unit.why: The main text describes the tsaddeket Hinda's nightly practice of tikkun hatzot and how she trained her small children in it. A footnote interleaved in the division tells a separate short anecdote: R. Zvi of Zhidachov, passing through Safrin, praised the village with a gesture.
unit.boundary_note: Footnotes (א)-(ג) are printed in the middle of the main sentence; the main text resumes after them with 'ה' בקדושה וטהרה'.

stories.start_quote: ושם אשת הרב רי"א הנז' היתה הצדיקת
stories.summary_en: Hinda, wife of R. Yitzhak Isaac of Safrin, rose every midnight to sit on the ground and say Tikkun Hatzot, and woke her small children to join her even when they cried, so they would get used to it.

quotes: ושם אשת הרב רי"א הנז' היתה הצדיקת
והקיצה תמיד גם את צאצאיה בהיותם ילדים קטנים
tags.why: The tsaddik's wife and children appear.

quotes: ולישב על הארץ לומר התיקון חצות
בקדושה וטהרה כחד מבני עליה המועטים
tags.why: Her holiness and purity in divine service.

quotes: ואף כי המה בוכים לא השגיחה ע״ז
tags.why: Rigorous austerity imposed even on crying children.
Framed as an oral tradition from the author's father.

stories.start_quote: וגם ידענו שזקינינו רבינו צבי הנז'
stories.summary_en: R. Zvi of Zhidachov, travelling through Safrin, turned his face back toward the village from his wagon. He said in Yiddish that not every forest produces such deer, and snapped his fingers.

quotes: בגדלותו נסע דרך ספרין וכשנסע מהכפר ומהיער
tags.why: The remark is made while the tsaddik travels.
He implicitly recognizes the holiness of the place and its people.

quotes: נישט פון אללע וועלדיר קומין ארויס אזעליכע הערשין
